The seventh and last left Nanjing in 1431, passed through Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and India, and reached Hormuz in the Persian Gulf. Part of the fleet went on to the east coast of Africa.

Thor Heyerdahl e cinco companheiros cruz: Thor Heyerdahl and five companions crossed the Pacific on a raft of balsa logs to show that South American peoples could have reached Polynesia. They left Callao, Peru, in April 1947, and after 101 days ran aground on the Raroia reef in the Tuamotu Islands.

Shackleton and five companions sailed about 1,300 km in the lifeboat James Caird to South Georgia and crossed the island on foot to get help. No one died.

Charles Lindbergh voou sozinho e sem esc: Charles Lindbergh flew solo and nonstop from New York to Paris in the Spirit of St. Louis on May 20–21, 1927. It took about 33.5 hours and covered 5,800 km over the North Atlantic.

The fleet sailed on to India, lost four ships in a storm near the Cape of Good Hope, including Bartolomeu Dias's, and reached Calicut in September.
A passagem do Cabo da Boa Esperança: Rounding the Cape of Good Hope
Bartolomeu Dias saiu de Lisboa em 1487 c: Bartolomeu Dias left Lisbon in 1487 with two caravels and a supply ship. After sailing down the African coast, a storm drove him away from land, and when he turned north again he found he had already passed the southern tip of Africa. He reached today's Eastern Cape and, on the way back, sighted the cape that King John II would name Good Hope. He opened the route Vasco da Gama would follow ten years later.
Viagem de Tasman ao continente do sul: Tasman's voyage to the southern continent
A serviço da Companhia Holandesa das Índ: Working for the Dutch East India Company, Abel Tasman left Batavia, today's Jakarta, in 1642 to search for the great southern continent. He was the first European to reach Tasmania and New Zealand, passed Tonga and Fiji, and returned to Batavia in 1643 north of New Guinea, circling Australia at a distance without ever sighting it.

Na segunda viagem, em 1535, Jacques Cart: On his second voyage, in 1535, Jacques Cartier sailed up the St. Lawrence River with three ships to the Iroquoian village of Stadacona, where Quebec City stands today, and went on by boat to Hochelaga, now Montreal. He wintered on the river, where many men died of scurvy until the Iroquoians taught them a tree-bark tea that cured it.
O jurista marroquino Ibn Battuta saiu de: The Moroccan jurist Ibn Battuta left Tangier in 1325 on pilgrimage to Mecca and only came home for good 29 years later. He traveled the Middle East, the east coast of Africa, Central Asia, India, where he served the Sultan of Delhi, the Maldives and China. Then he crossed the Sahara to the Mali Empire. He covered about 117,000 km, one of the longest distances traveled by anyone before the machine age.
Entre 1853 e 1856, David Livingstone atr: Between 1853 and 1856, David Livingstone crossed Africa from coast to coast: from the upper Zambezi he reached Luanda, on the Atlantic, came back the same way and followed the Zambezi down to Quelimane, on the Indian Ocean. Along the way, in November 1855, he became the first European to see the falls he named Victoria, which local peoples call Mosi-oa-Tunya, "the smoke that thunders".
Cerca de três anos · costa a costa: About three years · coast to coast
Na sua maior expedição, Henry Morton Sta: On his greatest expedition, Henry Morton Stanley left Zanzibar in 1874, circled Lake Victoria, explored Lake Tanganyika and descended the Lualaba River until he found it was the upper Congo. He followed the river to the Atlantic and reached Boma in August 1877. More than half of those who set out with him died or deserted along the way.

In February 1858 they reached Lake Tanganyika, the first Europeans to see it. On the way back, while Burton recovered in Tabora, Speke headed north and reached the great lake he named Victoria, which he believed, rightly, to be the source of the Nile.

The hardest part was descending the unknown River of Doubt, with rapids, hunger and disease that cost three men their lives. The river was renamed the Roosevelt River, and the expedition ended in Manaus.

They traveled up the Orinoco and confirmed its natural link with the Rio Negro through the Casiquiare Canal, crossed the Andes, got close to the top of Chimborazo in 1802, then thought to be the highest mountain in the world, and finished in Mexico, Cuba and the United States. Their accounts helped found modern geography.

Nansen deixou o Fram prender-se de propó: In 1893 Nansen let the Fram freeze into the ice north of Siberia on purpose, to prove that the Arctic current would carry the ship across the polar ocean. In 1895 he left the ship with Hjalmar Johansen and tried to ski to the Pole, reaching 86°14' N, the farthest north anyone had yet been. The two wintered in a stone hut in Franz Josef Land. The Fram broke free of the ice near Svalbard in 1896, as Nansen had predicted.

The claim is still disputed: to many scholars, the speeds recorded on the march seem too high.
Cerca de 37 dias de ida e volta no gelo: About 37 days out and back on the ice
Robert Falcon Scott e quatro companheiro: Robert Falcon Scott and four companions reached the South Pole on January 17, 1912, and found the tent Amundsen had left 34 days earlier. On the way back, Edgar Evans and Lawrence Oates died. Scott, Edward Wilson and Henry Bowers died trapped by a blizzard in March 1912, 18 km from a food depot.
A expedição de John Franklin saiu da Ing: John Franklin's expedition left England in 1845 with the ships Erebus and Terror and 129 men to complete the Northwest Passage. After a winter on Beechey Island, the ships became trapped in the ice near King William Island. Franklin died in 1847 and none of the men returned. The wreck of the Erebus was found in 2014 and that of the Terror in 2016.
Amelia Earhart e o navegador Fred Noonan: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan tried to fly around the world along the Equator in a Lockheed Electra. They left Oakland, passed through Miami, Natal, Dakar, Karachi and Singapore, and reached Lae, New Guinea, after about 35,000 km. On July 2, 1937, on the way to tiny Howland Island in the Pacific, they disappeared. No remains were ever found.

Primeiro voo ao Polo Sul: First flight to the South Pole

To gain altitude and clear the mountains on the climb up the Liv Glacier, they had to throw sacks of food out the door.

They used a sextant Coutinho had adapted for aviation, which let them navigate by the stars alone. The first plane sank at the Saint Peter and Saint Paul Archipelago, and two more were needed to finish the trip.

Finding a direct route to them was one of the great drivers of Portuguese and Spanish voyages.
